verdicts.note: S14 cuts both ways: alongside the 'race with China' framing and build incentives, he said concern about data centers is warranted, that 'people take a bit of a pause' and the industry 'needs to step forward', and he introduced a bill making data centers pay for the power and water systems they need so 'no community has a data center forced into it'. That is a regulatory requirement, not light-touch; the record is genuinely mixed.

Her own platform [S3] and pamphlet [S1] are incremental changes to the current system: restore Medicare/Medicaid funding, undo H.R. 1 eligibility rules, Medicaid for children under 19, drug-price negotiation. Single-payer appears only in one line of the Spokesman-Review's primary-night report [S4], not in her own words, which does not support the full pole_b position.

The evidence is opposition to a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors, with decisions left to patients and doctors and 'the parents should have a say' [S6], plus the general 'keep politicians out of your doctor's office' line [S1]. There is no explicit abortion-rights, sports or anti-discrimination position, so the full +2 pole is overstated.

missing.basis: Official site backs a 'patient-centered' system where Americans are not 'forced to follow bureaucratic directives', working within the existing structure (rural hospital fund) [S5]; he supports the H.R. 1 Medicaid eligibility restrictions as cost-cutting [S16]. Clearly not single-payer; -1 rather than -2 because pole_a's 'protect ACA/Medicaid' does not describe him.
